comment: Loved the class and found it quite easy. Consisted of a few projects/essay and was a bit less demandind due to the seminar style. Material can be a bit repetitive at times but the readings were super interesting as a psych major.

This class is BY FAR my favorite class I have taken at Richmond. People who complain are mostly Psyc majors who have never taken a science class in my opinion. Yes, there is a lot of information and you have to read outside class and study. However I think it is all very fair. The material is extremely fascinating and I loved this class.

Dr. Lambert is the smartest and most passionate professor I've had (she wrote the textbook). I think people only complain because it requires a lot of time outside class reading the textbook. There's no homework, 2-3 projects (easy As) and 3 tests (can be difficult) The second test we could use a notecard and the last one was half reflection based.

Dr. Lambert is super intelligent and passionate about the material. Only issue was her class was very lecture heavy and she didn't make the class engaging at all. Tests were difficult but we were allowed a note card since she knew the material is tough.
I strongly recommend every Psychology major student takes this, because i don't want to suffer from that alone :)

Dr. Lambert gave interesting, engaging lectures. You could tell she was passionate about the subject (especially when she got to talk about the area she specialized in). I retained a lot of the information despite the sheer amount of it because it was a survey course. Overall I really enjoyed the portion of the course that she taught.

If you want to do well in the class, you have to read the textbook. She also has you read the chapter before class and you turn in a reading assignment for it. The tests can be somewhat difficult. There are also a lot of reading/writing assignments due. Dr. Lambert is extremely kind and knowledgeable in the field & can be flexible with due dates.

Dr. Lambert is extremely knowledgeable in neuroscience. Definitely expects that you know the material. We were expected to read multiple studies and write a one page reflection of what was read each day. Multiple projects, presentations and papers were assigned throughout the semester that were all easy A's if you put in work to do them correctly.

She is a reasonable grader and lays out very detailed guidelines to how her external assignments need to be done. THAT being said, she assigns an excessive amount of work and tests on every single thing. She wrote the book she uses in class, so there's no hoping she won't focus on something. Retention is low because it is only memorization based.

So much reading that needs to be done, and the amount of sheer information in the class itself, and the tests, is a lot. She cant literally test you on anything and everything, even the smallest factoid mentioned in class.

Excessive amounts of reading in an unrealistically short timeframe (2-3 research papers per class (one was 80 pages long; an entire book in one week). Has homework due EVERY class. Changed the syllabus several times to add MORE projects/tests- midterm, final, 2 presentations, group projects. "Discussion" is mainly her talking at us for class time.
